output.summary: KEP-1024 proposes running a node-local DNS caching agent as a DaemonSet so pods reach a cache on their own node instead of the kube-dns service IP. The KEP is recorded as status implemented, stage stable, from 2020-12-16.
output.rationale: The design aims to cut DNAT and conntrack overhead, allow UDP-to-TCP upgrades to kube-dns, and give node-level DNS metrics. The discussion does not explain the original implemented decision; it concerns the later 2021 cleanup of KEP status fields (PR #3007). Reviewers debated whether this KEP should be "implemented" or "implementable" and whether PRR applied, since the KEP is out-of-tree and tied to prow. The sources do not record a final resolution specific to KEP-1024 beyond the recorded status.

alternatives.option: Service IP used as the nodelocaldns listen address
alternatives.why_not: Per the readme, this approach works only for iptables mode of kube-proxy, because ipvs mode binds all service IPs to a dummy interface and load-balances to endpoints, so the packets can be dropped when there are no endpoints.

alternatives.option: A nodelocaldns service with a same-node endpoint requirement
alternatives.why_not: The readme says this depends on same-node endpoint support (kubernetes/community PR 2846) that was not yet available when the KEP was written.

alternatives.option: Run a full kube-dns instance on every node
alternatives.why_not: The readme says this would consume much more resources, since each instance would also watch Services and Endpoints.

evidence.quote: This will consume much more resources since each instance will also watch Services and Endpoints.
It landed after https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/2672 (which made PRR required for implementable), but since it landed as implemented, it skipped PRR
Given that this KEP is related to prow, and not to anything that is contained in a kubernetes release, I think this is pretty uncontroversial
adds an extra validation check for `status:implemented == stage:stable`, it turns out nothing else violates this so I'd rather keep it as a rule
